hunks.baseline: It wasn’t difficult to figure out what the vibration was. I had something in my own pocket that made a similar sound, after all.

hunks.baseline: The fact that we were standing off against each other like this was absurd to begin with.

hunks.sol: The fact that we were facing off at all was absurd. No matter how gifted he was or how quickly he’d improved, he couldn’t stop me.

hunks.baseline: The only reason he was still standing there was entirely because I was holding back.
Holding back for a friend I would have no choice but to bring down.
hunks.sol: The only reason he was still on his feet was that I was letting him stay there. I was holding back for a friend I had no choice but to bring down.

hunks.baseline: And, in a way, it was restraint for a reason that made sense.
hunks.sol: And I had another reason to hold back.

hunks.baseline: “A call coming through on a direct line must be pretty important. Go ahead and answer it. I have to wait until enough witnesses gather anyway.”
hunks.sol: “If someone’s calling your direct line, it must be important. Go ahead and answer. I need to wait for enough witnesses to gather anyway.”

hunks.baseline: As I watched Team Leader Choi mull over those three syllables, I continued slowly.
hunks.sol: I watched Team Leader Choi turn the word over in his mind, then went on.

hunks.baseline: “Whatever happens from here on, the more people watching, the better. For everyone’s sake.”
hunks.sol: “The more people who see what happens next, the better. For all of us.”

hunks.baseline: Team Leader Choi and I had been in the same boat for a long time. If I killed Michael Silbert, it was obvious that Team Leader Choi would be dragged into it as one of my accomplices.

hunks.sol: Little by little, I’d learned not to look back.

hunks.baseline: Amid all the monsters that charged at me intent on killing me, and all the loathsome human crowds even worse than those monsters.

hunks.baseline: “This is the path I chose, and for now, it’s the best one.”

hunks.baseline: Sacrifice the Skeleton King, or hand this world over to Michael Silbert.
hunks.sol: Sacrifice the Skeleton King, or hand the world to Michael Silbert.

hunks.baseline: Faced with that impossible either-or, where I could not choose either option, I had made my decision.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t choose either. So I’d made a different decision.

hunks.baseline: Rather than being manipulated like a puppet, I would become a traitor who killed a hero and joined forces with a monster.
hunks.sol: Rather than let Michael control me like a puppet, I would kill a hero and become a traitor who had joined forces with a monster.

hunks.baseline: Even if that was what it took, I would uproot the source of this disaster.
hunks.sol: Even if that was what it took, I would tear out the root of this disaster.

hunks.baseline: *He’s going to die by my hand today.*
hunks.sol: *He dies by my hand today.*

hunks.sol: Heat spread through my body. I spat out the words as if I were chewing them to pieces, then unleashed the qi wave I’d drawn up to its limit.

hunks.sol: The force dwarfed anything Team Leader Choi had released. The hologram television, which had been playing silently, crackled and shut off. Alarms throughout the building began to wail.

hunks.sol: Footsteps hurried past the door. People shouted to one another. Team Leader Choi stared at me, looking hollow, then abruptly raised the *Hero’s Sword*.

hunks.sol: The silver blade sliced into the floor like tofu. He squeezed his eyes shut, opened them again, and pulled a smartphone and a potion from his clothes with the air of a man resigned to his fate.
